title: NEW COURSES AT TRIBHUVAN COOPERATIVE UNIVERSITY (TSU)
body_text:
The University launched three new MBA programmes during the academic year 2025–26:
MBA in Cooperative Management MBA in Cooperative Banking and Finance MBA in Agribusiness Management
The University has also designed five certificate courses for the professional management of cooperative societies. The names of these certificate courses are as follows:
Certificate Course in Business Management and Governance for the Secretaries and Staff of PACS (Primary Agricultural Credit Society) Certificate Course in Business Management and Governance for Secretaries and Staff of Primary Fisheries Cooperatives Certificate Course in Business Management and Governance for the Secretaries and Staff of Dairy Cooperative Societies Certificate Course in Leadership Development for the Board of Directors (BODs) of District Credit Cooperative Banks (DCCBs) Certificate Course in Cybersecurity for Cooperative Banks
The courses align with the need of PACS, Fisheries Cooperatives, Dairy Cooperatives and DCCBs.
While the new MBA programmes have been launched in 2025–26, the certificate courses are scheduled during 2026–27.
This information was given by Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation, Shri Amit Shah in a written reply in Rajya Sabha.
*****
AK/AP

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Cooperation informed Rajya Sabha that Tribhuvan Sahkari University (TSU) launched three new MBA programmes in 2025-26 — Cooperative Management, Cooperative Banking and Finance, and Agribusiness Management. The university has also designed five certificate courses for professional management of cooperative societies (covering PACS, fisheries cooperatives, dairy cooperatives, DCCB board leadership, and cybersecurity for cooperative banks), to be rolled out in 2026-27. Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Amit Shah gave this information in a written reply.
enrichment.context:
Tribhuvan Sahkari University (TSU) is India's first cooperative university, established under the Ministry of Cooperation (created in 2021) to build human resource capacity for the cooperative sector, which includes Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS), District Central Cooperative Banks (DCCBs), dairy and fisheries cooperatives. The Ministry has been pushing a broader agenda to revitalize and professionalize the cooperative movement, including computerisation of PACS, creation of new multi-purpose cooperative societies, and the '97th Constitutional Amendment' framework governing cooperative societies' autonomy and democratic functioning. Skill and management gaps at the grassroots level (PACS secretaries, DCCB boards) have long been cited as a reason for weak financial health and governance failures in cooperative institutions, especially cooperative banks which have faced RBI regulatory scrutiny after amendments brought them under stricter central bank oversight (2020 Banking Regulation Amendment Act).

These new MBA and certificate programmes are aimed at professionalizing management and governance across the cooperative credit and produce marketing ecosystem, addressing needs like financial literacy, cybersecurity (relevant given rising digital banking fraud), and leadership training for elected cooperative bank boards. This reflects a policy shift toward building specialized, sector-specific human capital rather than relying only on generic management or banking education, similar to how other sectors have dedicated skill universities (e.g. National Rail and Transportation Institute, Skill India Digital initiatives).

prelims_questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding Tribhuvan Sahkari University (TSU):
1. It is administered under the Ministry of Cooperation.
2. It has launched MBA programmes specifically in Cooperative Banking and Finance and Agribusiness Management.
3. Its certificate courses target only company secretaries of listed cooperative banks.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
prelims_questions.explanation: TSU is under the Ministry of Cooperation and has launched MBA programmes including Cooperative Banking and Finance and Agribusiness Management. The certificate courses target secretaries/staff of PACS, fisheries and dairy cooperatives, and BODs of DCCBs — not company secretaries of listed cooperative banks, so statement 3 is incorrect.

prelims_questions.question: The abbreviation 'PACS', frequently referenced in cooperative sector reforms, stands for which of the following?
prelims_questions.explanation: PACS stands for Primary Agricultural Credit Society, the grassroots-level cooperative credit institution in India providing short-term agricultural credit to farmers.
